Telemetry Basics
What telemetry is and what to do when Telemetry Nurse calls.

What is Telemetry?

A wireless system used for continuous monitoring of a patient's cardiac rhythm and heart rate.

If Telemetry Nurse calls about an arrhythmia

  1. Assess the patient first. Check condition, symptoms and vital signs as appropriate.
  2. Review the rhythm. Correlate the finding with the patient's clinical condicontent">

    Pay attention to new/significant rhythm changes

    • Chest pain
    • Shortness of breath
    • Syncope or near-syncope
    • Hypotension
    • Altered level of consciousness
    Workflow: Assess → Review rhythm → Notify/Escalate according to condition and hospital policy.
🔌
Electrode Placement
Essential checks for reliable ECG signal quality.

Quick check

  • Use the approved 5-lead placement: R, L, C2, C5, F, N.
  • Electrodes properly attached.
  • Skin clean and dry.
  • Leads correctly connected.
  • Replace electrodes according to hospital policy.
Visual Guide: Follow the approved lead placement and telemetry cable connection shown below.
Key reminder: Ensure the connector is fully inserted and the tracing is clear.
🔄
Quick Flowchart
A simple “What should I do?” pathway.
📞 Telemetry notification→👀 Assess patient→❤️ Symptoms/Vitals→🫀 Do ECG
📈 Review rhythm→🔌 Check leads if needed→📞 Escalate→📝 Document

Telemetry Nurse Reminders
Quick reminders for connecting, managing, and returning telemetry devices.
  • Connect telemetry within 15 minutes of receiving the request.
  • Do not delay telemetry after Echo, Cath Lab, CT, or other procedures.
  • After receiving the device, call Telemetry Station 14709 to verify the device number, patient name, and URN.
  • Double-check patient identifiers before attaching the device.
  • Change ECG electrodes every shift and ensure the device is functioning/charging.
  • Report any ECG changes immediately to the doctor.
  • Call back the requesting department after telemetry connection.
  • If the primary nurse is unavailable, the charge nurse should ensure telemetry is connected.
  • On discharge, return the telemetry device within the same shift.
  • Clean and return the device before requesting another one; use the borrower slip/sticker.
  • Secure telemetry and IV cables to prevent falls.
  • If the patient refuses telemetry: inform the doctor to explain its importance; if refusal continues, obtain a signed Refusal Form and document it.
📝 Unified PN Documentation

Received telemetry device from Telemetry Station. Device No. ___. Verified by read-back with TN and attached to the patient after double-checking patient identifiers.

At handover

  • Confirm telemetry is still connected and the correct device is with the correct patient.
  • Communicate any recent rhythm changes, concerns, or pending actions.
🖼️
How to Verify the Correct Patient on Telemetry
Step-by-step guide to verify the correct patient and telemetry device.

Verify before attaching the device

  1. Press the upper menu/button on the telemetry device to display the patient information.
  2. Verify Name + URN/MRN shown on the device.
  3. Match the identifiers with the patient's ID band.
  4. Confirm the device number with Telemetry Station using closed-loop communication.
Do not rely on room or bed number alone. Verify the patient using approved identifiers.
